newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols drift as futures struggle.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols drift as futures struggle.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options ended little changed Tuesday as upside momentum in the underlying futures stalled.

Options traders said bond volatilities upticked in the morning when September futures looked on track to break above the 111-00 mark. When futures fell short, turning lower on the day and gravitating back toward the recent trading range, vols also drifted back, the traders said.
September volatility ended at about 8.35 percent, up 0.5 percentage point from Monday's close. July slipped to 7.60 percent by the end of the day from 7.70 percent previously.

July volatility has now returned to where it was valued before Friday's May employment report, between 7.5 percent and 8.0 percent, when futures were range-trading around 109-00 to 110-00, one U.S. brokerage trader noted.

September has retained a slight bid because the lifespan of the options covers the July and August Federal Open Market Committee meetings, he said. The FOMC meets July 1-2 and then again on August 19, and the options' last trading day is August 22.
Today's options activity mostly consisted of liquidation of July contracts, which expire in less than two weeks, and rollover of positions into September, floor traders said.
One sizable transaction that stood out was a futures firm's sale of 3,000 July 111-00 bond calls.
In addition, market participants were still trying to clean up options positions after Friday's volatile session caught many traders off guard, said a floor trader for a U.S. banking firm.

The mild early losses that followed the jobs number on Friday prompted some traders to sell July options premium, a strategy that backfired when futures reversed direction midday and staged a dramatic rally, the bank trader said.

July volatility's retreat below 8.0 percent suggests market participants are not expecting more fireworks later this week, the bank trader said. May U.S. retail sales are scheduled for release Thursday, followed by the May producer price index on Friday.
In Eurodollar options, traders said volatility was flat to down 0.1 percentage point across the board, with December pegged at about 10.7 percent.
